name: enumerate()
what_it_does: Pairs each item of an iterable with its index, so a for loop can access both the position and the value at the same time.
parameters: iterable - what to loop over. start (optional) - the number to begin counting from, defaults to 0.
return_value: An enumerate object that yields (index, value) tuples - usually unpacked directly in a for loop.
common_mistakes: Manually tracking an index with a separate counter variable (`i = 0; for x in items: ...; i += 1`) when enumerate() does it directly and can't get out of sync. Forgetting you can pass start=1 instead of adding 1 to the index yourself.
when_to_use: Any time a loop needs to know the position of the current item, e.g. printing a numbered list or building index-value pairs.
